questions.question: How is security risk commonly assessed?

options.A: By the number of testers who are available to perform security testing on the product
options.B: By the likelihood that a threat exploits a vulnerability combined with the impact
options.C: By the number of lines of source code in the application that is being assessed
options.D: By the amount of money that the organization spent on security tools last year

questions.explanation: Risk combines how likely it is that a threat exploits a weakness with how severe the consequences would be. Effort, code size or spending do not measure it.

questions.question: What does the attack surface of a system consist of?

options.A: The list of all users who have ever logged in to the system in the past
options.B: Only the parts of the system that were written by the internal development team
options.C: All the points where an attacker can try to enter data or extract data
options.D: The physical dimensions of the servers on which the application is hosted

questions.explanation: The attack surface is the sum of the entry and exit points, such as interfaces, ports, inputs and services. A smaller surface generally means fewer opportunities for attackers.

questions.question: What is a zero-day vulnerability?

options.A: A flaw that is unknown to the vendor, so no patch exists yet
options.B: A flaw that only exists on the day when the software is first released
options.C: A flaw that can be fixed in less than one day by any experienced developer
options.D: A flaw that has been listed in a public database for many years already

questions.explanation: A zero-day is a weakness for which the vendor has had no time to prepare a fix, which makes exploitation particularly dangerous until a patch or workaround is available.

questions.question: What is the difference between CVE and CWE?

options.A: CVE classifies types of weaknesses, while CWE identifies specific known vulnerabilities
options.B: CVE is a security test tool, while CWE is a standard for writing test reports
options.C: CVE identifies specific known vulnerabilities, while CWE classifies types of weaknesses
options.D: CVE and CWE are two names for the same list, maintained by different vendors

questions.explanation: A CVE entry names a particular vulnerability in a product, while a CWE entry describes a category of weakness, such as improper input validation, that can occur in many products.

questions.question: What distinguishes a computer worm from a virus?

options.A: A worm is harmless software that only slows down computers for a short time
options.B: A worm spreads by itself across networks, without needing a host file to be run
options.C: A worm is a type of firewall rule that blocks all incoming network connections
options.D: A worm can only spread when a user shares a file on a removable storage device

questions.explanation: Worms replicate and propagate autonomously, often through network vulnerabilities, whereas viruses attach to files and need a user or process to run the infected host.

questions.question: In a man-in-the-middle attack, what does the attacker do?

options.A: Intercepts and possibly alters communication between two parties who believe they talk directly
options.B: Guesses passwords by trying every possible combination of characters until one works
options.C: Floods a server with so many requests that legitimate users can no longer be served
options.D: Sends an email with a malicious attachment to a large group of employees at once

questions.explanation: The attacker positions between the communicating parties to eavesdrop or modify data. Encryption with proper certificate validation is a main countermeasure.

questions.question: What is the difference between horizontal and vertical privilege escalation?

options.A: Horizontal gives higher privileges, while vertical gives access to another user's resources at the same level
options.B: Horizontal happens only on networks, while vertical happens only on individual devices
options.C: Horizontal is done by the tester, while vertical is done only by the system administrator
options.D: Horizontal gives access to another user's resources at the same level, vertical gives higher privileges

questions.explanation: In horizontal escalation an attacker reaches data of peers, such as another customer's account. In vertical escalation the attacker obtains higher rights, such as administrator functions.

questions.question: What characterizes a brute-force attack on authentication?

options.A: Reading the credentials from network traffic that is not encrypted
options.B: Systematically trying many possible credentials until one is accepted
options.C: Exploiting a flaw in the code that skips the password check completely
options.D: Tricking a user into revealing a password by pretending to be a colleague

questions.explanation: Brute force relies on trying large numbers of guesses. Lockouts, rate limiting and strong passwords reduce its chances of success.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical objective of security testing?

options.A: Measuring how quickly users can learn to operate the software interface
options.B: Proving that the software contains no vulnerabilities of any kind whatsoever
options.C: Finding vulnerabilities and verifying that security controls work as intended
options.D: Reducing the cost of the software licenses that are used by the organization

questions.explanation: Security testing aims to reveal weaknesses and confirm the effectiveness of controls. Testing cannot prove the complete absence of vulnerabilities.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: What is the purpose of compliance-oriented security testing?

options.A: To check that the system meets the requirements of applicable regulations, standards or policies
options.B: To improve the performance of the system under a heavy load of simultaneous users
options.C: To find as many vulnerabilities as possible regardless of any regulation or policy
options.D: To decide which programming language is used for the development of the software

questions.explanation: Compliance testing gathers evidence that mandatory requirements, such as those from standards or laws, are fulfilled. Meeting them does not by itself guarantee that the system is secure.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: How does a security audit differ from security testing?

options.A: An audit and security testing are the same activity performed under two different names
options.B: An audit mainly reviews processes and evidence against a policy, while testing exercises the system
options.C: An audit is always performed by the developers, while testing is always performed by outsiders
options.D: An audit executes attacks against a live system, while testing only reads documents

questions.explanation: Audits assess whether controls and processes conform to a policy or standard, largely through review. Security testing actively checks the behavior of the system for weaknesses.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: What information does a tester have in gray-box security testing?

options.A: No knowledge of the system at all, apart from its public address
options.B: Complete knowledge of the system, including all of the source code and designs
options.C: Partial knowledge of the system, such as architecture details or limited credentials
options.D: Knowledge only of the color scheme and layout of the user interface

questions.explanation: Gray-box testing sits between black-box and white-box, using some internal information to make testing more efficient while still viewing the system from the outside.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: Why is independence of the security testers often valuable?

options.A: Independent testers never need to receive any information about the system
options.B: Independent testers can bypass the rules and agreements that govern the test
options.C: Independent testers are always cheaper than testers who work in the project team
options.D: Independent testers are less influenced by assumptions made during design and development

questions.explanation: A fresh perspective helps find flaws that authors overlook because of shared assumptions. Independence does not remove the need for scope, agreements or information.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: How can legal and regulatory requirements affect security testing?

options.A: They apply only to physical buildings and never to software or data
options.B: They remove the need to plan security tests because the law already guarantees security
options.C: They allow testers to attack any system they can reach without any permission
options.D: They can restrict what data may be used and which systems may be tested, and require authorization

questions.explanation: Laws on data protection and unauthorized access shape how tests may be carried out, so scope, data handling and permissions must be agreed beforehand.

questions.question: Which topic belongs in a security test plan?

options.A: Only the passwords of the systems that are going to be tested
options.B: Scope, objectives, approach, resources, schedule and handling of findings
options.C: Only the price list of the tools that could be bought in the future
options.D: Only the list of names of all employees who work in the organization

questions.explanation: A plan states what will be tested and how, by whom and when, and how findings are treated. Credentials belong in controlled handover, not in the plan.

questions.question: What is an attack tree used for in security test design?

options.A: To list the employees of the organization according to their rank in the hierarchy
options.B: To store the source code of the application in a hierarchical directory structure
options.C: To show the physical layout of the network cables inside the data center
options.D: To model the ways an attacker could reach a goal, so that test cases can be derived from the paths

questions.explanation: An attack tree breaks an attacker's goal into sub-goals and alternative paths. Each path can inspire test conditions and helps prioritize by likelihood and effort.

questions.question: Why should security tests that might disrupt services be run in an isolated test environment?

options.A: To ensure that the testers cannot see any of the results of their own tests
options.B: To avoid having to obtain any permission for the tests from system owners
options.C: To avoid harming production systems and real users while testing hazardous attacks
options.D: To make sure that the results of the tests are always identical to production

questions.explanation: Aggressive tests such as fuzzing or denial-of-service attempts can crash systems and corrupt data. An isolated environment contains the impact, though it should resemble production as far as possible.

questions.question: Why should security test execution be logged in detail?

options.A: To replace the need for a test report at the end of the testing activity
options.B: To make the tests run more slowly so that the systems are not overloaded
options.C: To provide evidence, allow findings to be reproduced, and support later analysis
options.D: To increase the number of tests that are recorded as executed in the metrics

questions.explanation: Logs of actions, inputs and responses let others verify and reproduce results and show what was covered. They complement, but do not replace, reporting.

questions.question: Which is a suitable exit criterion for security testing?

options.A: The application has been running for exactly one week without any reported problems
options.B: All planned tests executed and no open findings above an agreed severity threshold
options.C: The test team has run out of coffee and is unable to continue with the work
options.D: The number of executed tests equals the number of employees in the company

questions.explanation: Exit criteria link completion to coverage of planned tests and to the state of findings. Arbitrary times or unrelated numbers say nothing about risk.

questions.question: What does traceability between risks and security tests provide?

options.A: Evidence of which identified risks have been covered by tests and which have not
options.B: A list of all testers ranked according to the number of defects they found
options.C: A guarantee that every risk has been eliminated from the system that was tested
options.D: A method for automatically fixing the vulnerabilities that testing has revealed

questions.explanation: Linking risks to tests shows coverage of what matters most and highlights gaps. It does not remove the risks or fix vulnerabilities.

questions.question: What kind of test data is preferred for security testing?

options.A: Only very short inputs that consist of a single letter or digit each
options.B: Data that is chosen at random without considering what is being tested
options.C: Synthetic or properly anonymized data, plus deliberately crafted malicious inputs
options.D: Unmodified copies of real customer data taken from the production database

questions.explanation: Using real personal data creates privacy risk, so synthetic or masked data is used. Security tests also need specially crafted inputs such as injection strings and boundary values.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a testable security requirement?

options.A: The system should keep data safe against any possible attack of the future
options.B: The system locks an account for 15 minutes after five consecutive failed logins
options.C: The system must be very secure and easy for all users to work with
options.D: The system will be developed by developers who care about security

questions.explanation: A testable requirement is specific and verifiable, such as a lockout after a defined number of failures. Vague statements cannot be checked objectively.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Which secure design principle states that access should be denied unless explicitly granted?

options.A: Convenience first
options.B: Security through obscurity
options.C: Open design by default
options.D: Fail-safe defaults

questions.explanation: Fail-safe defaults means that in the absence of an explicit permission, access is refused. This limits the damage of configuration mistakes and missing rules.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: What is a benefit of a security-focused code review?

options.A: The code no longer needs to be tested dynamically once the review is complete
options.B: The code becomes faster because reviewers remove all of the comments
options.C: Weaknesses such as missing validation can be found before the code is ever executed
options.D: The reviewers can automatically fix every defect while reading the source code

questions.explanation: Reviews reveal insecure constructs early and cheaply. They complement dynamic testing, which observes actual runtime behavior, and do not replace it.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Why are security tests at unit level valuable?

options.A: They can only be used to test the network configuration of the servers
options.B: They replace the need for any testing of the integrated system in later phases
options.C: They are able to detect every kind of social engineering attack on the users
options.D: They find weaknesses such as improper input handling early and cheaply

questions.explanation: Unit-level tests, for example for validation routines, find defects close to their source. Later levels are still needed to find integration and configuration issues.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Why should acceptance criteria for a user story include security aspects?

options.A: So that only the security team can accept or reject any story in the backlog
options.B: So that security expectations are verified as part of the definition of done
options.C: So that the stories can be written without describing any functional behavior
options.D: So that the story is guaranteed never to be completed by the development team

questions.explanation: Security criteria in the acceptance criteria make security a normal part of delivery and prevent it from being an afterthought that is postponed indefinitely.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: What is the idea of DevSecOps regarding security testing?

options.A: Separating development and security teams so that they never communicate
options.B: Performing all security testing manually once at the end of each year
options.C: Removing security testing from the process to speed up releases
options.D: Integrating automated security checks into the delivery pipeline

questions.explanation: DevSecOps embeds security into development and operations, for example through scanners in the CI pipeline, so weaknesses are detected close to when they are introduced.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: What is a software bill of materials (SBOM) useful for?

options.A: Listing the employees who worked on the software and the hours that they spent
options.B: Knowing which components and versions the software contains, to identify known vulnerabilities
options.C: Calculating how much money the software will earn during its first year of sale
options.D: Documenting the colors and fonts that are used in the user interface

questions.explanation: An SBOM inventories components and their versions, which lets teams quickly check whether a newly announced vulnerability affects them.

questions.question: What is system hardening?

options.A: Reducing the attack surface, for example by disabling unused services and changing default settings
options.B: Giving every user administrator rights so that no one is blocked in their work
options.C: Making the physical casing of the servers thicker so that they resist impact
options.D: Installing as many additional applications as possible on the servers of the system

questions.explanation: Hardening removes unnecessary functions, accounts and open ports and applies secure configuration, which leaves fewer ways in for attackers.

questions.question: How does a stateful firewall differ from a simple packet filter?

options.A: It tracks the state of connections and decides based on the context of the traffic
options.B: It works only on the application and never on the network connections
options.C: It allows all traffic to pass and only records what happened afterwards
options.D: It examines only the color of the packets that pass through the network cable

questions.explanation: A stateful firewall remembers established connections and evaluates packets in that context, whereas a simple packet filter judges each packet in isolation based on header fields.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a demilitarized zone (DMZ) in network design?

options.A: To connect the internal network directly to the internet without any protection
options.B: To store the backups of the data on the same server as the live database
options.C: To place public-facing services in a separate segment, isolated from the internal network
options.D: To give all users unrestricted access to all resources in the organization

questions.explanation: A DMZ hosts exposed services so that if one is compromised, the attacker still has to pass another barrier to reach internal systems.

questions.question: What is the main difference between an intrusion detection system and an intrusion prevention system?

options.A: There is no difference, because both terms describe the same behavior in every product
options.B: A detection system blocks traffic, while a prevention system only creates alerts
options.C: A detection system works only offline, while a prevention system works only online
options.D: A detection system alerts on suspicious activity, while a prevention system can also block it

questions.explanation: IDS monitors and reports, IPS sits in the traffic path and can drop or block malicious activity. Testing should check both detection and the intended response.

questions.question: What is the EICAR test file used for?

options.A: Checking that anti-malware software detects a harmless standard test signature
options.B: Measuring the speed of the internet connection of the test environment
options.C: Storing the passwords of the users of the anti-malware software
options.D: Infecting a system with a real virus to see how it behaves

questions.explanation: The EICAR file is a harmless string that scanners are designed to flag as if it were malware, so testers can verify detection without using real malicious code.

questions.question: What does data masking do?

options.A: Replaces sensitive values with realistic but fictitious ones
options.B: Copies sensitive values into a second table where everyone can read them
options.C: Encrypts all data with a key that is printed on the cover of the database
options.D: Deletes the entire database so that no test can ever use any data

questions.explanation: Masking or obfuscation protects confidential information in non-production use. Testers should verify that masked data cannot be reverted to the originals easily.

questions.question: Which combination is an example of multi-factor authentication?

options.A: A password together with a security question known to the user
options.B: A password together with a code from a hardware token
options.C: Two different usernames typed into the same login form
options.D: A password together with a second password of the same kind

questions.explanation: Multi-factor authentication combines different factor types: something you know, something you have, and something you are. Two passwords are the same factor.

questions.question: Why is hashing, not reversible encryption, appropriate for storing passwords?

options.A: Encryption cannot be used with passwords because they contain special characters
options.B: Hashing makes passwords shorter so that less storage space is needed for them
options.C: The system only needs to verify a password, so the original never has to be recoverable
options.D: Hashed passwords can be turned back into text for the user by the administrator

questions.explanation: Verification only requires comparing hashes of the entered and stored values. Not being able to recover the original limits damage if the store is stolen, especially with salting.

questions.question: What does role-based access control (RBAC) do?

options.A: Grants permissions to each user individually and never uses groups of any kind
options.B: Lets every user decide who else may access the resources that they can see
options.C: Grants permissions to roles, and users obtain permissions by being assigned to roles
options.D: Removes all permissions from users so that nobody can access anything

questions.explanation: In RBAC, permissions are attached to roles such as clerk or manager. Testing checks that each role gets what it should and no more, and that role assignments are enforced.

questions.question: What must a tester verify about TLS certificate handling in a client application?

options.A: That the client accepts every certificate so that connections never fail
options.B: That the client ignores certificates and sends data in unencrypted form
options.C: That the client rejects invalid, expired or untrusted certificates
options.D: That the client displays the certificate as an image on the login screen

questions.explanation: Without proper validation, an attacker can present a fake certificate and intercept traffic. Tests should confirm that invalid certificates lead to refused connections.

questions.question: Which of the following is a social engineering technique?

options.A: Guessing passwords by trying all combinations with a program
options.B: Flooding a web server with requests until it can no longer respond
options.C: Tailgating, following an authorized person through a secured door
options.D: Exploiting a buffer overflow in a network service

questions.explanation: Tailgating manipulates people rather than technology. The other options are technical attacks against systems.

questions.question: How can the effectiveness of security awareness training be assessed?

options.A: By asking the trainers whether they were satisfied with their own lessons
options.B: By measuring behavior, such as click rates in simulated phishing
options.C: By checking whether the employees attended the training in their free time
options.D: By counting how many training slides were shown to employees in total

questions.explanation: Attendance and content volume do not show that behavior changed. Simulations and reported incidents measure whether people act more securely.

questions.question: What is meant by a security culture in an organization?

options.A: A department that alone is responsible for every security matter
options.B: Shared attitudes and behaviors of taking responsibility for information
options.C: A technical tool that automatically blocks every form of attack
options.D: A list of rules that are stored in a folder and never read by anyone

questions.explanation: Culture reflects what people actually do. Rules or tools alone do not create it, and security responsibility is shared, not delegated to a single department.

questions.question: Why should employees have an easy way to report suspicious emails?

options.A: Reporting is only necessary when the email contains a virus attachment
options.B: Reports make the number of emails that the employees receive smaller
options.C: Reports are used to blame employees who click on links by mistake
options.D: Quick reports allow security staff to react and warn others before an attack spreads

questions.explanation: A simple reporting channel turns users into sensors. Early warnings help contain campaigns, and a blame-free approach encourages people to report.

questions.question: Why can insiders be a significant security threat?

options.A: They only cause harm through natural disasters that affect the building
options.B: They are always outside the organization and therefore cannot be identified
options.C: They have no access to the systems, so they must find a way to break in
options.D: They already have legitimate access and knowledge of the systems and processes

questions.explanation: Insiders can misuse legitimate rights, deliberately or by mistake, which perimeter controls do not stop. Least privilege, monitoring and separation of duties help.

questions.question: What should a security test report typically contain?

options.A: Only the source code of the tools which the testers used
options.B: Only a statement that the system is secure, without any supporting detail
options.C: Scope, approach, findings with severity, evidence and recommendations
options.D: Only the names of the testers and the times that each of them worked

questions.explanation: A useful report explains what was tested and how, what was found, how serious it is, how to reproduce it and what to do about it.

questions.question: Which factors influence the severity rating of a vulnerability?

options.A: Ease of exploitation, impact on the CIA attributes, and asset exposure
options.B: The day of the week and the time on which the vulnerability was found
options.C: The color of the report and the font size which the tester chose for it
options.D: The number of pages which the description of the finding needs

questions.explanation: Severity reflects how easily an attacker can exploit the flaw, what damage would result and how accessible the affected asset is.

questions.question: Which metric shows how quickly vulnerabilities are being resolved?

options.A: Mean time to remediate, measured from reporting to verified fix
options.B: The length of the security policy document in pages
options.C: The number of tools that the security team has installed
options.D: The total number of security tests that exist in the repository

questions.explanation: Time to remediate shows responsiveness to findings, and it can be tracked by severity to see whether the most serious issues are handled first.

questions.question: Why should a finding include steps to reproduce it?

options.A: So that developers can verify and fix the problem, and testers can confirm the fix
options.B: So that other attackers are able to repeat the attack on the same system
options.C: So that the report becomes as long as possible and appears more thorough
options.D: So that the finding can be closed without any further investigation

questions.explanation: Reproducible findings save analysis time and avoid disputes, and the same steps are used during retesting. Reports must be protected because they show how to attack.

questions.question: How should a security test report be stored and distributed?

options.A: With restricted access on a need-to-know basis, protected by encryption
options.B: On a public web page so that everyone can learn from the findings
options.C: On any shared drive that is available without a password
options.D: By email to the entire company to make sure that all employees are informed

questions.explanation: Reports describe unfixed vulnerabilities and could help attackers. Access should be limited to those who need it, and the content protected in storage and transit.

questions.question: What does it mean when a business owner accepts a residual risk?

options.A: They knowingly accept the remaining risk instead of fixing it, and document that
options.B: They ask the testers to remove the finding from the report so it is not visible
options.C: They transfer responsibility for the risk to the testers who discovered it
options.D: They confirm that the vulnerability no longer exists after a successful fix

questions.explanation: Risk acceptance is a documented decision by an accountable owner, based on understanding the risk. It is not deletion of the finding or a shift of responsibility to testers.

questions.question: What is a botnet?

options.A: A set of firewall rules that block traffic from known malicious countries
options.B: A collection of backups that are stored on servers in different locations
options.C: A network of compromised devices controlled remotely by an attacker
options.D: A group of testers who run security tests together against a target system

questions.explanation: A botnet consists of infected machines that follow commands from an attacker, and is often used for denial-of-service attacks, spam and credential attacks.

questions.question: What characterizes a Trojan horse?

options.A: A program that spreads across networks by itself without any interaction from users
options.B: A backup copy of a program that is stored on a separate server
options.C: Malicious software that pretends to be something useful to trick users into running it
options.D: A firewall setting that blocks all traffic from unknown network addresses

questions.explanation: A Trojan relies on deception, hiding harmful functions inside a seemingly legitimate program, and typically does not replicate on its own.

questions.question: What is the typical goal of ransomware?

options.A: To test the strength of the passwords which users have chosen
options.B: To silently observe user behavior in order to improve the software
options.C: To make data or systems unavailable until a payment is made
options.D: To speed up the computer by removing unnecessary files

questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts or locks data and demands payment for its release. It mainly threatens availability, and often confidentiality as well when data is stolen.

questions.question: What is the aim of a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack?

options.A: To modify the data in a database without leaving any trace in the logs
options.B: To overwhelm a service with traffic from many sources at once
options.C: To steal the passwords of users by watching their keyboard input
options.D: To force users to install an update that contains a hidden backdoor

questions.explanation: A DDoS uses many systems, often a botnet, to exhaust bandwidth or resources, which threatens availability.

questions.question: What does responsible (coordinated) disclosure of a vulnerability mean?

options.A: Informing the vendor first and allowing time for a fix before publishing details
options.B: Selling the details of the vulnerability to the highest bidder without telling anyone
options.C: Publishing all details immediately on the internet so that everyone knows about it
options.D: Keeping the vulnerability secret forever and never telling the vendor about it

questions.explanation: Coordinated disclosure balances transparency with protection: the vendor gets a chance to fix the flaw before attackers can exploit publicly known details.

questions.question: What is the difference between a passive and an active attack?

options.A: A passive attack is done at night, while an active attack is done during the day
options.B: A passive attack changes data, while an active attack only observes information
options.C: Passive attacks only observe, while active attacks change data or behavior
options.D: A passive attack is done by insiders, while an active attack is done by outsiders

questions.explanation: Eavesdropping on traffic is passive and hard to detect, whereas tampering with messages or injecting requests is active and often leaves traces.

questions.question: Which list correctly names the three main types of security controls by their function?

options.A: Internal, external and hybrid
options.B: Preventive, detective and corrective
options.C: Physical, mental and emotional
options.D: Fast, medium and slow

questions.explanation: Preventive controls stop incidents, detective controls discover them, and corrective controls limit damage and restore normal operation. Tests should cover each kind.

questions.question: What is spoofing?

options.A: Pretending to be another user, device or system to gain access
options.B: Removing the log files from a system after an attack has ended
options.C: Crashing a program by sending it an unexpectedly large input
options.D: Encrypting the data of a victim so that it cannot be read anymore

questions.explanation: Spoofing falsifies an identity, such as an email sender or an IP address. Strong authentication helps to counter it.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: How does risk influence the depth of security testing?

options.A: Only areas with no risk are tested, because they are the easiest
options.B: All areas are tested exactly the same regardless of their importance
options.C: Areas with higher risk receive more thorough testing than areas with lower risk
options.D: Risk has no influence on testing, which depends only on the schedule

questions.explanation: Risk-based testing directs limited effort to assets and functions where a successful attack would hurt most or would be most likely.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: Why is a combination of test approaches often used in security testing?

options.A: Combining approaches makes it impossible for anyone to reproduce the results
options.B: A single approach always finds all vulnerabilities, so combinations are unnecessary
options.C: Combinations are used only when the budget for testing is unlimited
options.D: Different approaches find different kinds of weaknesses, so together they give better coverage

questions.explanation: Static analysis, dynamic scanning and manual testing each have strengths and blind spots, so a mix reduces the chance of missing important weaknesses.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: How do security standards and regulations support test planning?

options.A: They replace the need for any test planning because they contain all the tests
options.B: They forbid the use of automated tools in any security testing activity
options.C: They apply only to hardware and never to the software that runs on it
options.D: They provide requirements and controls from which test conditions can be derived

questions.explanation: Standards and regulations state what must be protected and which controls are expected, giving a basis for test objectives and coverage.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A tester would like to test a cloud service used by the organization but operated by another company. What is required?

options.A: Permission from the provider and adherence to its testing rules
options.B: Nothing, because any system that can be reached may be tested
options.C: A note in the internal test plan that the provider is informed
options.D: The approval of the testers' own manager only

questions.explanation: Testing systems that belong to others without authorization can be illegal. Providers usually define what is allowed, and the scope must respect this.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: What are misuse or abuse cases used for in security testing?

options.A: Describing the steps for installing the system on a server
options.B: Listing the features that the marketing department wants to promote
options.C: Describing how an attacker might deliberately misuse the system, to derive tests
options.D: Describing how the normal users will use the system in their daily work

questions.explanation: Misuse cases are the negative counterpart of use cases. They help think like an attacker and lead to test conditions for unwanted behavior.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: Why must the cost of security testing be weighed against the value of what is protected?

options.A: Because resources are limited and effort should be proportionate to the risk
options.B: Because more expensive tests always find more vulnerabilities than cheaper ones
options.C: Because the value of the protected assets never changes over time
options.D: Because security testing is only allowed if it costs nothing at all

questions.explanation: Proportionality guides investment: high-value or high-risk assets justify deeper testing, while low-risk items may get only basic checks.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: Why should security testing also check detection and response capabilities?

options.A: Because detection is only useful after the system has been shut down
options.B: Because response teams are not allowed to see the results of tests
options.C: Because attacks cannot always be prevented, so they must be noticed and handled quickly
options.D: Because prevention controls never work and are therefore not worth testing

questions.explanation: Defense includes prevention, detection and response. Tests confirm that alerts fire and that people and processes react, limiting the damage of successful attacks.

questions.question: What is the role of risk analysis at the beginning of the security test process?

options.A: It replaces the execution of tests with a theoretical discussion
options.B: It removes the need for any further planning of the tests
options.C: It is used only to decide the color of the report at the end
options.D: It identifies what needs protection and which threats matter

questions.explanation: Risk analysis supplies the basis for choosing test focus, depth and techniques. Without it, effort might go to areas of low importance.

questions.question: Why are boundary values and equivalence classes also useful for security tests?

options.A: Inputs at and beyond limits often reveal overflows and validation gaps
options.B: They are used only to test the color contrast of the screens
options.C: They make sure that every possible attack is covered by one test
options.D: They are the only techniques which are allowed in security testing

questions.explanation: Classic techniques apply to security: unusually long, empty or malformed inputs near or beyond limits test how well validation and error handling work.

questions.question: What is fuzzing?

options.A: Interviewing the users about how they feel about the security of the system
options.B: Reading the source code line by line to find errors in the logic
options.C: Comparing the system against a checklist of the compliance requirements
options.D: Providing large numbers of malformed or random inputs to find crashes and weaknesses

questions.explanation: Fuzzers automatically generate unexpected inputs and monitor the target for failures, which is effective at finding memory and parsing defects.

questions.question: Why is monitoring the target system during security test execution important?

options.A: Crashes or odd logs can indicate a vulnerability even without visible failure
options.B: Monitoring makes the tests pass more often than they would without it
options.C: Monitoring replaces the need to record any test results
options.D: Monitoring is only used to measure how fast the tester is typing

questions.explanation: Many security problems show up only in logs, resource use or behavior behind the scenes, so observation beyond the visible response is needed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of lessons learned at the end of a security test project?

options.A: Assigning blame to the person who made the most mistakes
options.B: Proving that no improvements to the process are possible
options.C: Deleting all the information about the test to save storage
options.D: Improving future testing by identifying what worked and what did not

questions.explanation: A structured review of the test process yields improvements for planning, techniques, tools and cooperation in later projects.

questions.question: Which factor influences the effort required for a security test?

options.A: The size and complexity of the target and the required depth of testing
options.B: The name of the city where the company was originally founded long ago
options.C: The favorite color of the person who signs the invoice for the testing work
options.D: The number of pictures that appear on the company's public website

questions.explanation: Scope, complexity, required depth and available information affect effort. Unrelated facts do not.

questions.question: Which is a criterion when selecting a security testing tool?

options.A: The tool has the longest name of all the tools on the market
options.B: The tool has never been used by any other organization
options.C: The tool is recommended by the person who talks the loudest in meetings
options.D: Suitability for the target technology and fit with the existing process

questions.explanation: Tools should fit the technology, skills and workflow, and support reporting. Popularity or novelty alone is not a valid reason.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Why should abuse cases be considered during requirements analysis?

options.A: Requirements can address how the system might be attacked, not just used
options.B: Abuse cases are only considered after the system has been released
options.C: Abuse cases are needed only for systems that have no users
options.D: Abuse cases replace all functional requirements in a project

questions.explanation: Considering attackers early leads to requirements such as lockouts and validation, which are cheaper to build in than to add later.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: What is checked in a security design review?

options.A: Whether the developers work overtime on the weekend
options.B: Whether the test cases are written in the correct language
options.C: Whether the color choices of the interface are pleasant to the users
options.D: Whether the architecture applies security principles and covers the threats

questions.explanation: A design review examines trust boundaries, data flows and controls, so that structural weaknesses can be corrected before implementation.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Which best describes static analysis for security?

options.A: Measuring the response time of the application under load
options.B: Examining code or binaries without executing them to find weaknesses
options.C: Running the application with attack inputs and observing its behavior
options.D: Interviewing the users about their experience with the software

questions.explanation: Static analysis inspects code automatically or manually and can find issues early, although it may report false positives and cannot see runtime configuration.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Why is testing at the interfaces between components important for security?

options.A: Interfaces are used only to display graphics to the user
options.B: Interfaces never contain defects because they are simple
options.C: Trust boundaries are crossed there, and data may be accepted unvalidated
options.D: Interfaces are the only parts which can contain security defects

questions.explanation: When data crosses from one component or system to another, assumptions about trust can be wrong, making interfaces a frequent source of vulnerabilities.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: What is the value of security testing in a production-like environment during system testing?

options.A: The tests can be executed without any test environment
options.B: Deployment and configuration issues that developer setups hide can be found
options.C: The results are guaranteed to be identical to those of the unit tests
options.D: Production data can be changed freely without any consequences

questions.explanation: Security depends on configuration, network and infrastructure, which a production-like environment reproduces better than a development machine.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Why is regression testing needed after applying a security patch?

options.A: To remove the need for testing the patch itself
options.B: To prove that the software will never need another patch
options.C: To delete the older versions of the software from the server
options.D: To confirm the fix works and did not break other functions or controls

questions.explanation: Patches can introduce side effects. Regression tests check the fixed behavior and the surrounding functionality, including existing security controls.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Why should incident response procedures be exercised in the operations phase?

options.A: To replace the monitoring of the production systems
options.B: To find gaps in detection and recovery before a real incident happens
options.C: To make sure that no incident will ever occur in the future
options.D: To reduce the number of employees in the security team

questions.explanation: Exercises such as tabletop or simulated attacks show whether people and tools work together under pressure and reveal weaknesses in the plans.

questions.question: What is the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption?

options.A: Symmetric works only for images, while asymmetric works only for text
options.B: Symmetric uses one shared key, while asymmetric uses a public and private key pair
options.C: Symmetric uses a key pair, while asymmetric uses one shared secret key
options.D: Symmetric is always slower and therefore used for all large amounts of data

questions.explanation: Symmetric algorithms use the same key to encrypt and decrypt and are fast. Asymmetric algorithms use related keys, which helps with key exchange and signatures.

questions.question: What does a digital signature provide?

options.A: Secrecy of the message content for all recipients in every case
options.B: Evidence of who created a message and that it has not been altered
options.C: Protection against a denial-of-service attack on the sender
options.D: Faster delivery of the message over the network

questions.explanation: A signature made with a private key can be verified with the public key, providing authenticity and integrity, and supporting non-repudiation.

questions.question: How is forced browsing tested?

options.A: By requesting URLs of protected resources directly without proper authorization
options.B: By changing the resolution of the screen while using the application
options.C: By running the application on an older version of the browser
options.D: By disabling the images in the browser settings

questions.explanation: Forced browsing checks whether access control is applied to every resource, not merely hidden by the absence of links in the interface.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a port scan in security testing?

options.A: To remove unused files from the file system of the server
options.B: To measure how fast a user can type in the login form
options.C: To identify which network services are reachable on a system
options.D: To check the spelling in the documentation of the application

questions.explanation: A port scan reveals open ports and services, allowing verification that only intended services are exposed as part of hardening.

questions.question: What is the difference between an authenticated and an unauthenticated vulnerability scan?

options.A: They are the same, because scanners never use credentials
options.B: An authenticated scan works only on paper documents
options.C: An unauthenticated scan logs in, while an authenticated scan does not
options.D: An authenticated scan logs in and sees internal configuration

questions.explanation: Scans with credentials inspect patch levels and settings from the inside and give more accurate results, whereas unauthenticated scans show the outside view an anonymous attacker has.

questions.question: How should audit logs be protected?

options.A: By allowing every user to edit the entries that concern their own actions
options.B: By deleting them every hour to save disk space on the server
options.C: By storing them in the same directory that users can write to
options.D: Against unauthorized modification and deletion, such as with restricted access

questions.explanation: If attackers or insiders can alter logs, evidence is lost. Testers verify that logging cannot be tampered with and that entries are complete.

questions.question: What does a web application firewall (WAF) do?

options.A: Backs up all of the web pages to a remote location every night
options.B: Filters HTTP traffic to block common web attacks such as injection
options.C: Encrypts all of the database files that are stored on the servers
options.D: Checks the physical access badges of visitors to the data center

questions.explanation: A WAF operates at the application layer, inspecting requests and responses against rules. Testers check whether it blocks attacks, and know that it does not replace fixing vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Why is key management important for encryption?

options.A: Keys should be stored next to the encrypted data for easy access
options.B: Keys should be shared with all employees so that they can decrypt the data
options.C: Keys are not needed because encryption algorithms work without them
options.D: Even strong encryption fails if keys are exposed, poorly generated or never rotated

questions.explanation: The security of encryption depends on secret keys. Generation, storage, distribution, rotation and destruction must all be handled and tested.

questions.question: What should be tested about session timeouts?

options.A: That inactive sessions expire and cannot be reused after the timeout or logout
options.B: That the sessions are shared between all users of the application
options.C: That the session identifier is displayed on every page of the application
options.D: That sessions last as long as possible, whatever the user does

questions.explanation: Sessions that never expire give attackers a longer window to hijack them. Testing confirms expiry and server-side invalidation.

questions.question: How do signature-based and heuristic malware detection differ?

options.A: Signature-based detects new malware only, while heuristic detects known malware only
options.B: Signature-based detects known patterns, while heuristic looks for suspicious behavior or structure
options.C: They are the same technique described with different words
options.D: Signature-based needs no updates, while heuristic needs updates every second

questions.explanation: Signatures catch known threats precisely but miss new variants. Heuristics can flag unknown threats but may produce false positives.

questions.question: What distinguishes spear phishing from ordinary phishing?

options.A: It happens only by telephone and never by email
options.B: It is sent to millions of random addresses without any customization
options.C: It targets specific people using personal information to seem credible
options.D: It is performed only by the employees of the organization

questions.explanation: Spear phishing tailors the message to a person or group, which makes it more convincing and harder to spot than mass phishing.

questions.question: What is pretexting?

options.A: Inventing a believable scenario to get someone to reveal information
options.B: Encrypting messages with a secret pattern before sending them
options.C: Forwarding messages automatically to a shared mailbox
options.D: Testing a text editor before it is released to customers

questions.explanation: In pretexting, an attacker builds a false story, such as posing as support staff, to gain the target's trust and get something they should not have.

questions.question: What does a baiting attack involve?

options.A: Sending thousands of requests to a web server at the same time
options.B: Leaving something enticing, such as an infected USB stick
options.C: Guessing the password of an account with a list of common words
options.D: Intercepting the wireless signals of a nearby network

questions.explanation: Baiting exploits curiosity or greed. Awareness training and technical controls, such as disabling autorun, reduce the risk.

questions.question: Why is shoulder surfing a concern for security testers?

options.A: It damages the hardware of the computers that people are using
options.B: People can observe secrets such as passwords on screens or keyboards
options.C: It only affects people who work from home on personal laptops
options.D: It slows down the network in large open offices with many users

questions.explanation: Shoulder surfing is a low-tech way to steal information in public or open places. Privacy screens and awareness help counter it.

questions.question: What ethical rule applies to security testers?

options.A: Work only within the agreed scope and keep discovered information confidential
options.B: Share the findings with anyone who asks, in order to be transparent
options.C: Use any vulnerability found for personal gain if nobody notices
options.D: Ignore the scope whenever something interesting is found

questions.explanation: Testers hold sensitive access and knowledge. Professional conduct means respecting authorization limits and protecting the information that they encounter.

questions.question: What should an executive summary of a security test report focus on?

options.A: The personal opinions of the testers about the developers
options.B: The complete output of the tools used, without any interpretation
options.C: The detailed technical steps of each attack in the order which they were performed
options.D: The overall risk level, key findings and business impact in non-technical language

questions.explanation: Executives need to understand risk and decisions required. Technical details belong in the body of the report or appendices.

questions.question: How should findings in a report be ordered?

options.A: In alphabetical order of the names of the affected components
options.B: In the order that the tests happened to be executed by the tester
options.C: Randomly, so that no finding is seen as more important
options.D: By severity or priority, so the most important issues are seen first

questions.explanation: Prioritized findings help stakeholders focus remediation on the most serious risks first.

questions.question: Why should false positives be removed or marked before a report is delivered?

options.A: They increase the severity of the real findings in the report
options.B: They are required by law to be removed from the reports
options.C: They waste the time of developers and reduce trust in the report
options.D: They make the report shorter, which is always an advantage

questions.explanation: Scanner output contains items that are not real vulnerabilities. Validating findings keeps reports credible and remediation effort focused.

questions.question: What can trend analysis of security findings over several releases show?

options.A: The exact date and time on which the next attack will happen
options.B: Whether the testers are happy in their work and with their pay
options.C: How many new users will buy the product in the following year
options.D: Whether vulnerabilities are becoming fewer or more severe

questions.explanation: Trends across releases indicate the effect of secure development and testing practices, and help decide where to invest further.

questions.question: What should be documented about a retest of a fixed vulnerability?

options.A: Nothing, because a fixed vulnerability no longer matters to anyone
options.B: Whether the fix was verified, how it was tested, and what remains
options.C: Only that a retest was performed, without listing any results
options.D: Only the name of the developer who wrote and deployed the fix

questions.explanation: Retest results close the loop: they confirm the fix, record the evidence and highlight whether the weakness or a variant persists.

questions.question: What makes a recommendation in a security report practical?

options.A: It blames the developers and does not suggest a fix
options.B: It describes concrete corrective actions that the responsible team can carry out
options.C: It demands replacing the entire system, whatever the size of the issue
options.D: It says only that the system must be made secure, without giving details

questions.explanation: Actionable recommendations describe what to change, where and why, and can be prioritized. Vague or disproportionate advice is rarely implemented.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: Which stakeholder normally decides whether a remaining security risk is acceptable?

options.A: The vendor that supplied the scanning tool used to discover the weakness
options.B: The tester who found the vulnerability during the security test activity
options.C: The help desk employee who received the first call about the problem
options.D: The owner of the business asset or process that is exposed to the risk

questions.explanation: Accepting risk is a business decision made by whoever is accountable for the asset, informed by the test results. Testers advise but do not accept risk on the owner's behalf.
